See runnerRegistry.ts's own evidence refresh for why `correlation` now carries only `actionKey`. (2) checkEditActionProviderPathGateV1 is restructured: it now resolves the stage's effective provider FIRST, and only when that resolves to Copilot does it ALSO run checkEditActionHostGateV1() and return its result — previously (this same round) it always returned `{ok:true}` for a resolvable CLI model, but every command wrapper still called the unconditional, provider-independent checkEditActionHostGateV1() as its own separate first statement BEFORE ever reaching this function, so a CLI-resolved stage on a host missing the Copilot LM tool API (or below 1.100) was still incorrectly rejected — the advertised CLI direct-edit path was unreachable on exactly the hosts where only the Copilot pipeline should have been unavailable. Every caller in reviewActions.ts, fastForwardCurrentTaskReview.ts, and this file's own resumeEditPreflightInteractionV1 now calls only the single merged checkEditActionProviderPathGateV1(stage) — the separate preceding checkEditActionHostGateV1() call is removed at each site (see their own evidence refreshes). checkEditActionHostGateV1 stays exported for applyImplementationReviewWithAI's defense-in-depth check, which now guards it with its own already-resolved model's provider kind instead of calling it unconditionally. Evidence refresh 2026-08-05 second pass (Codex review fix, second round, two changes): (1) runImplementationOrSealedV1's CLI branch now passes `allowCrossProviderBackups: false` to runImplementationForModel (see runnerRegistry.ts's own evidence refresh) — without it, a CLI primary's failed run could silently hand off to a configured Copilot backup through the older, unsealed Copilot runner, bypassing the sealed pipeline's host gate/preflight/receipts entirely for that backup attempt. (2) resumeEditPreflightInteractionV1 gains a new local requireCopilotForResumeV1(modelId), used at both its checkpoints in place of checkEditActionProviderPathGateV1/checkEditActionAvailabilityV1's now-CLI-permissive behavior: a pending edit-preflight interaction was, by construction, raised by the sealed pipeline (CLI never creates one — ImplementationRunResult has no "questions" outcome), so Resume is Copilot-only even though a fresh invocation now has a valid CLI path. Without this, if the stage's model was switched to CLI after the interaction was raised, coordinator.resumeAction would be reached with a CLI-resolved model: its `preflight` mode has no CLI support, so it would settle (consume) the pending interaction as a terminal providerModeUnavailable failure with no way to retry it, and if a Copilot backup were also configured, the coordinator's own provider selection could instead run that backup's sealed mutation session against a model whose host floor was never validated (the host gate only ever checked the CLI primary). requireCopilotForResumeV1 rejects up front, before coordinator.resumeAction is ever called, with a message telling the user to configure a Copilot model or start a fresh run instead. Evidence refresh 2026-08-05 third pass (Codex review fix, third round: options.modelId is the stage's CONFIGURED CLI primary, not necessarily an installed one — this branch dispatched it as-is, so a primary that is simply not installed classified as failureKind "generic" inside runImplementationForModel, which only cascades to ITS OWN backup list on "quota"/"temporarily-unavailable"; a configured, available backup was therefore never attempted, even though checkImplementationAvailabilityForModel (already called by upstream callers, e.g. executeImplementationRun's own liveness re-check) had already found it available and used its label in the (suppressed) warning): runImplementationOrSealedV1 now calls checkImplementationAvailabilityForModel(options.modelId, stage) itself, ONLY after confirming the primary is CLI-resolved (a Copilot-resolved primary is unchanged — still dispatches straight to runSealedImplementationV1 with no new pre-check), and dispatches the WINNING candidate's modelId instead of options.modelId. If that winning candidate is itself CLI-resolved, it runs through runImplementationForModel as before (allowCrossProviderBackups: false, unchanged); if the CLI primary was unavailable but a configured Copilot backup is, that backup is routed through runSealedImplementationV1 (with the backup's modelId) rather than runImplementationForModel's unsealed Copilot branch, preserving the same sealed-pipeline-only guarantee for Copilot that allowCrossProviderBackups protects inside the cascade. Verified by manual trace of classifyCliFailure (a "command not found" message resolves failureKind "generic", confirmed in utils/quota.ts) and by the full existing suite; no new dedicated test was added for this specific redirect because the CLI existence probe cache (cliAgentRunner.ts's commandExistsCache, keyed by command name, 60s TTL, no test-reset hook) makes a clean two-command differentiated-availability fixture fragile to add safely alongside the existing spawn-mocked suite without further investment — a plain risk left recorded here rather than silently absent. Evidence refresh 2026-08-05 fourth pass (Codex review fix, fourth round, two changes): (1) checkEditActionProviderPathGateV1 is now itself async and availability-aware, mirroring runImplementationOrSealedV1's own resolution: it resolves the stage's configured primary's WINNING candidate via checkImplementationAvailabilityForModel (the primary if live, else the first available configured backup, of either kind) before deciding whether the Copilot host check applies — a CLI-primary/Copilot-backup stage previously skipped that check entirely (checking only the primary's kind), so a host-incompatible Copilot backup's mismatch surfaced only deep inside runImplementationOrSealedV1 itself, after resolveTask and every artifact/context-pack read this gate exists to precede (AC-HOST-03). resolveEffectiveProvider(modelId) is still checked first, outside checkImplementationAvailabilityForModel's own unguarded internal call to it, so an unconfigured/unresolvable model still fails closed with a clean result instead of throwing. All 5 call sites (reviewActions.ts x3, fastForwardCurrentTaskReview.ts, this file's own requireCopilotForResumeV1) now await it — see their own evidence refreshes; fastForwardReviewWithAI's early gate is additionally moved inside its knownTargetsImplReview !== false branch, since the gate is no longer zero-I/O and a plan-review-only invocation must not pay for it. Covered by a new runEditActionV1.test.ts case proving the gate accepts a live Copilot backup behind a not-installed CLI primary, and rejects when that backup itself lacks the required host capability. (2) requireCopilotForResumeV1 gains the identical fix and a new `stage` parameter: it previously checked only the raw modelId's kind, so an interaction legitimately raised by a Copilot backup (while the primary stayed CLI) became permanently unresumable — Resume would reject on the primary's kind alone, even with the exact same backup still live. It now resolves the winning candidate the same way before requiring Copilot, re-verified fresh at Resume time (the interaction transaction does not record which candidate actually created it, so this follows the same 're-check liveness right before use' precedent already used throughout this file). Both call sites pass the stage they already compute. Evidence refresh 2026-08-05 fifth pass (external reviewer, one nit on the same round): runImplementationOrSealedV1's unresolvable-model failure hardcoded `runnerId: "copilot-lm"` regardless of what options.modelId actually was — log noise only (resolution had already failed, so nothing dispatched), but misattributed a CLI-prefixed id's failure to Copilot in run logs. Now derives a best-effort label from the stored id's own "<provider>:" prefix when it has one, falling back to "copilot-lm" only for a bare/undefined selection (which genuinely does default to Copilot). Evidence refresh 2026-08-06 (Codex review fix, sixth round, closing a gap the third pass's own "unchanged — still dispatches straight to runSealedImplementationV1 with no new pre-check" scoping left behind): runImplementationOrSealedV1 now calls checkImplementationAvailabilityForModel(options.modelId, stage) unconditionally, for a Copilot-resolved primary too, and dispatches on the WINNING candidate's provider kind rather than the PRIMARY's. The third-pass scoping only ran this check for a CLI-resolved primary, on the reasoning that a Copilot primary's own gates were a sufficient contract for it — but that left the opposite fallback direction dead: a Copilot primary that is itself unavailable, with a configured "switch-to-backup" CLI candidate, never reached the availability check at all (the CLI-only condition short-circuited straight to runSealedImplementationV1(options) with the original, unavailable Copilot modelId), so the CLI backup was configured but structurally unreachable — this is the same asymmetry independently reported by review-msgk3b48-riafph's P2 finding on this same function. For a healthy, backup-free primary of either kind this changes nothing observable: availability.modelId === options.modelId and dispatch lands on the identical call as before.
